findings.text: REQ-4 depends on counting rules in PRD DSH-5..DSH-7, which are not inputs. A tester has no criterion to check beyond 'same as the other tiles'. This is handled by U-1/Q-01 but stays loosely testable.

rubric_items.reason: All six acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-10. The motivation in L13-L14 (follow-up, per-doctor/day spotting) is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable, and AC4 and AC6 are split correctly. REQ-4 ('counted the same way') cannot be tested on its own because the counting rule lives in PRD rules that are not inputs.
Every REQ marked known cites a ticket line, and no values are invented. The missing PRD rules are recorded as U-1 rather than assumed.
There is no direct clash between ticket and baseline. The baseline goal 'shows the day in one screen' (cited as C3) against the 7/30-day periods is not discussed.
Two non-blocking questions, each with real options and sensible defaults. Both go to the tech lead, which fits a code-behaviour question and a glossary question.
Plain language. No-show and Medical history are used as the glossary defines them, and undefined terms are flagged.
